'''NumWorks''' is a French [[technology company]] that designs, develops, and sells [[graphing calculator]]s. Their calculators are [[source-available]] and have their hardware design available under a [[Creative Commons license]].<ref name="ChS3Y">{{cite web|title=Open Source Calculator Teaches us about Quality Documentation|url=https://hackaday.com/2018/05/18/open-source-calculator-teaches-us-about-quality-documentation/|last1=Scharfglass|first1=Kerry|date=May 18, 2018|website=Hackaday|access-date=April 2, 2019|archive-date=April 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190402233041/https://hackaday.com/2018/05/18/open-source-calculator-teaches-us-about-quality-documentation/|url-status=live}}</ref> Its first calculator, the N0100, was released on August 29, 2017, in Europe and the United States and is geared towards high school classrooms and students.<ref name="MfstV">{{Cite web|last1=Dent|first1=Steve|date=August 28, 2017|url=https://www.engadget.com/2017/08/28/numworks-graphing-calculator/|title=NumWorks graphing calculator is made for students raised on tech|website=Engadget|access-date=February 24, 2019|archive-date=February 4, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204063041/https://www.engadget.com/2017/08/28/numworks-graphing-calculator/|url-status=live}}</ref> The calculators use Python as their programming language, rather than a proprietary language (e.g. [[TI-BASIC]], which is used by Texas Instruments calculators).

== Development ==
Romain Goyet, the CEO of NumWorks, started the company in 2016. Before starting NumWorks, he was a software engineer at [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] who also contributed to open-source projects such as [[Linux]].<ref name="adafruit">{{Cite web|url=https://blog.adafruit.com/2018/05/25/adafruit-interviews-numworks-python-programmable-calculator-micropython/|title=Adafruit interviews NumWorks – Python Programmable calculator #micropython|last=Barela|first=Anne|date=May 25, 2018|website=Adafruit Industries - Makers, hackers, artists, designers and engineers!|access-date=March 6, 2019|archive-date=July 30, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190730162102/https://blog.adafruit.com/2018/05/25/adafruit-interviews-numworks-python-programmable-calculator-micropython/|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Products ==
The NumWorks [[graphing calculator]] was the first graphing calculator to be [[Programmable calculator|programmable]] using the [[Python (programming language)|Python]] language. It features a 320x240 IPS display with a 2.8″ diagonal. Internally, it is powered by a 216&nbsp;MHz [[ARM Cortex-M|Cortex-M7]] processor and 8 MB of [[Serial Peripheral Interface|Quad-SPI]] [[Flash memory]]. The calculator has a 1450 mAh [[lithium polymer battery]]. The calculator weights {{convert|5.9|oz|lbs|abbr=on}} and measures {{convert|8.2|x|16|x|1|cm|in|abbr=on}}.

Four versions of the calculator were produced by NumWorks: the N0100 model, the N0110 model, the N0120 model, and the N0115 model. Technical limitations of the N0100 model's memory prevent any upgrade to an OS version higher than 19.5.17.

== Features ==
The calculator was specifically designed to be modded using 3D printing. 3D models, schematics, and board layout details are available to the public under a Creative Commons license.<ref name="adafruit" /> The software on the calculator is updated on a monthly cycle. Updates can be downloaded to the calculator from its website using [[WebUSB]] or by building the operating system from its direct source.

The NumWorks calculator also includes various "exam modes" which may disable certain features (e.g. the periodic table app, Python scripts, etc.) in accordance with regional exam regulations. Exam mode can be disabled by plugging the calculator into a power source and selecting disable on the popup that appears.

On March 22, 2019, NumWorks released an app for iOS and Android, free of charge.<ref name="4VbX1">{{Cite tweet |user=numworks |number=1109032300849885184 |date=March 22, 2019 |title=Pour bien finir la semaine, une nouveauté que vous avez été nombreux à nous demander : votre calculatrice NumWorks est désormais disponible gratuitement sur iPhone et sur Android! |language=fr |access-date = April 2, 2019}}</ref> It features the same functionality as the physical calculator except it does not have [[Persistent data structure|data persistence]].
